round1Questions.question: In which year did Srila Prabhupada board the Jaladuta to travel to America?
round1Questions.explanation: Srila Prabhupada boarded the Jaladuta cargo ship in August 1965 at age 69.

round1Questions.question: What is the full name of ISKCON?
round1Questions.explanation: ISKCON was incorporated in New York in July 1966.

round1Questions.question: Which scripture did Srila Prabhupada translate and comment on, calling it the 'ripened fruit of the tree of Vedic literature'?
round1Questions.explanation: Prabhupada described Srimad Bhagavatam as the ripened fruit of the Vedic desire tree.

round3Questions.question: Why Dhrtarastra had the fear of losing the battle? (BG 1.1)
options: Because the battle was to take place at dharma-ksetra, which is a place of pilgrimage
Because pandavas were virtuous by nature
round3Questions.explanation: Dhrtarastra feared both the sanctity of the holy place and the virtue of the Pandavas.

round3Questions.question: What is the significance of the words dharma-ksetre and kuru-ksetre apart from their historical and Vedic importance? (BG 1.1)
options: In the field of Kuruksetra the father of religion is Krishna
In the field of Kuruksetra unwanted plants like Dhrtarastra's son Duryodhana and others would be wiped out
In the field of Kuruksetra religious persons headed by Yudhisthira would be established by the Lord
round3Questions.explanation: All three meanings are given in the purport to BG 1.1.

round3Questions.question: Why Duryodhana pointed out Dronacarya's mistake in relation to his disciple Dhrstadyumna, the son of Drupada? (BG 1.3)
options: So that Dronacarya is alert and uncompromising in the fighting
So that Dronacarya is not lenient in the battle against Pandavas
So that Dronacarya's such leniency if be any, would lead to defeat of Duryodhana's party
round3Questions.explanation: Duryodhana wanted Dronacarya alert, non-lenient, and feared leniency would cost him the battle.

round3Questions.question: On account of the presence of great warriors on Duryodhana's party like Bhisma and others, what was his conclusion on the result of the battle? (BG 1.9)
options: He was confident of his victory
He was also doubtful of his victory like his father
round3Questions.explanation: 'Aparyaptam tad asmakam balam' — despite Bhisma, he harboured doubt like his father.

round3Questions.question: Duryodhana after praising Bhisma as a far superior general, why asks others to support him? (BG 1.11)
options: Because he wanted everyone to feel important
Because he didn't wanted anyone to be felt neglected
round3Questions.explanation: He wanted each commander to feel important and none neglected in defending Bhisma.

tieBreakerQuestions.explanation: Dhrtarastra asks Sanjaya what his sons and the Pandavas did at Kuruksetra (BG 1.1).
